subject.title: [Feature]: Pre-reset agentic memory flush — /new and daily reset should get the same memory flush as compaction

question: Should OpenClaw run a silent tool-capable memory-flush agent turn before explicit, daily, and idle resets, and what blocking/background/config rules should govern it?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the permanent behavior affects latency, silent agent execution, sensitive memory persistence, and plugin/config contracts, so automation should not choose the policy alone.

options.title: Approve a bounded pre-reset flush
options.body: Define a default policy with timeout, dedupe, opt-out/config, audit, sandbox, and security constraints before a focused implementation.

options.title: Keep reset persistence mechanical
options.body: Treat session-memory or reset-hook improvements such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/61675 as the supported reset boundary and narrow this issue away from silent agent execution.

options.title: Delegate to memory plugins
options.body: Require external memory plugins or MCP-backed services to own continuous persistence and only extend core lifecycle APIs where current plugin hooks are insufficient.

recommendation.title: Approve a bounded pre-reset flush
recommendation.body: Define a default policy with timeout, dedupe, opt-out/config, audit, sandbox, and security constraints before a focused implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest combined history on the pre-compaction flush primitive and /new reset behavior that this decision spans.
